Your spine isn't one long bone — it's made of many small stacked bones called vertebrae!

What gives skin its color?

Skin color comes from melanin — the more melanin you have, the darker your skin, and it also helps block the sun's harmful rays.

Ano ang nagbibigay kulay sa balat?

Ang kulay ng balat ay galing sa melanin — mas marami ang melanin, mas maitim ang balat, at ito rin ang humaharang sa masamang sinag ng araw.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghatag kolor sa panit?

Ang kolor sa panit gikan sa melanin — kung daghan ang melanin, mas itom ang panit, ug kini usab ang nagsumpo sa makadaot nga sidlak sa adlaw.

What else does your skin do?

Your skin isn't just a covering — it's also an excretory organ. Millions of sweat glands release sweat that removes heat and some waste.
copy.tl:
Ano pang ginagawa ng balat mo?

Ang balat mo ay hindi lang panlabas na takip — organo rin ito ng excretion. Milyun-milyong sweat glands nito ang naglalabas ng pawis na nagtatanggal ng init at ilang basura.
copy.bis:
Unsa pa ang buhaton sa imong panit?

Ang imong panit dili lang tabon — excretory organ usab kini. Milyun-milyong sweat glands niini ang nagpagawas og pawis nga nagtangtang sa init ug pipila ka basura.

Your skin! If you spread it out flat, it would cover almost two square meters, because it wraps around your whole body.

Ano ang pinakamalaking organ ng katawan?

Ang balat! Kung ikakalat mo ito nang patag, sasakop ito ng halos dalawang metro kuwadrado dahil binabalot nito ang buong katawan mo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga organo sa lawas?

Ang panit! Kon ibukhad kini nga patag, motabon kini og halos duha ka metro kwadrado kay giputos niini ang tibuok nimong lawas.

Why don't small bumps hurt us badly?

Under our skin is a layer of fat that acts like a soft cushion, absorbing bumps and knocks so our organs and bones stay safe.

Sa ilalim ng ating balat ay may patong ng taba na parang malambot na unan, na sumasahod sa mga banggaan para hindi agad masaktan ang ating mga laman-loob at buto.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili dayon kita masakitan sa bunggo?

Sa ilalom sa atong panit naay sapaw sa tambok nga sama sa humok nga unlan, nga nagsalo sa mga bunggo aron dili dayon masakitan ang atong mga sulod nga organo ug bukog.

How does sweat cool you down?

Your skin protects you from overheating through sweat. When sweat evaporates off your skin, it cools your body so you don't get too hot inside.

Pinoprotektahan ka ng balat mo sa sobrang init sa pamamagitan ng pagpapawis. Kapag sumisingaw ang pawis sa balat, lumalamig ang katawan mo.
copy.bis:
Giunsa ka pabugnawa sa singot?

Ang imong panit manalipod nimo batok sa sobrang init pinaagi sa singot. Kon mosingaw ang singot sa panit, mobugnaw ang imong lawas.

When does a skink actually drop its tail?

Dropping the tail is a last resort — the skink only does it when there's no other way to escape, since it costs the body a lot.

Kailan lang lumulusot ang buntot ng skink?

Ang paghulog ng buntot ay huling paraan lamang — ginagawa ito ng skink kapag wala nang ibang paraan para makatakas, dahil malaki ang gastos nito sa katawan.

Kanus-a ra mahulog ang ikog sa skink?

Ang pagpahulog sa ikog mao lamang ang kataposang paagi — buhaton kini sa skink kung wala nay laing paagi aron makaikyas, kay dako kini og bayad sa lawas.

How do you keep a loaded skylab from tipping over?

Arrange the load evenly to keep its balance! If one side is too heavy, it easily tips over.

Ayusin nang patas ang kargada para sa balanse! Kung mabigat ang isang gilid, madali itong tumagilid.

Unsaon pagpugong sa pagtakilid sa nakargang skylab?

Ihan-ay nga patas ang karga aron sa balanse! Kon bug-at ang usa ka kilid, dali kining motakilid.

copy.en:
Is a slug a snail without a shell?

A slug is just like a snail, but it has no hard shell — that's why its body is soft!
copy.tl:
Kuhol ba na walang shell?

Ang slug ay parang kuhol, pero wala itong matigas na shell — kaya malambot ang katawan nito!
copy.bis:
Kuhol ba nga walay kabhang?

Ang slug sama sa kuhol, apan walay gahi nga kabhang — busa humok ang lawas niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Smaller pieces dissolve faster than one big lump because more surface is exposed to the water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses dissolution rate due to surface area, not solubility (maximum amount that can dissolve) nor the factor heat named in the competency. It shares the topic of dissolving but does not directly support demonstrating factors affecting solubility.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Smaller pieces dissolve faster than one big lump because more surface is exposed to the water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses dissolution rate, not the classification of uniform vs non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. It does not describe mixture types or provide useful everyday examples of solutions/suspensions.

copy.en:
Why do crushed pieces dissolve faster?

Smaller pieces dissolve faster than one big lump because more surface is exposed to the water!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabilis matunaw ang mga dinurog na piraso?

Mas mabilis matunaw ang maliliit na piraso kaysa sa malaking bukol dahil mas malaki ang nakalantad na ibabaw!
copy.bis:
Nganong mas paspas matunaw ang mga dinugmok nga tipik?

Mas paspas matunaw ang gagmay nga tipik kaysa sa dakong bukol kay mas dako ang nabutyag nga ibabaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bones heal more slowly when a person lacks good nutrition or has certain health problems.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bones and healing but does not describe how the skeletal system (or any other body system) works. It only states a factor that affects bone healing, which is not the competency's focus.

copy.en:
Why do some broken bones heal slower?

Bones heal more slowly when a person lacks good nutrition or has certain health problems.
copy.tl:
Bakit mabagal maghilom ang ilang buto?

Mas mabagal maghilom ang buto kapag kulang sa wastong nutrisyon o may ibang sakit ang tao.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga hinay maayo ang pipila ka bukog?

Mas hinay maayo ang bukog kon kulang sa hustong nutrisyon o adunay laing sakit ang tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: smoking weakens the lungs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs but does not identify respiratory system parts from pictures/diagrams or describe how they work. It focuses on a health effect of smoking, not the structure or function of the respiratory system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: smoking weakens the lungs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs and breathlessness but does not describe how the respiratory system works. It does not support the competency's requirement to describe the functioning of body systems.

copy.en: A smoker gets out of breath and tired quickly when running or playing, because smoking weakens the lungs!
copy.tl: Ang naninigarilyo ay madaling humingal at mapagod sa pagtakbo o paglalaro dahil mahina na ang baga nito!
copy.bis: Ang nagapanigarilyo dali rang maghangak ug kapuyon sa pagdagan o pagdula tungod kay luya na ang baga niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A few kinds of snails are predators that eat other snails or worms, though most snails we know munch on plants.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that some snails eat other snails/worms (carnivorous behavior) and most eat plants (herbivorous behavior), but it does not use the terms herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore, nor does it group animals according to the food they eat. It provides a single example rather than supporting the grouping skill required by the competency.

copy.en:
Do all snails eat only plants?

Not all of them! A few kinds of snails are predators that eat other snails or worms, though most snails we know munch on plants.
copy.tl:
Halaman lang ba ang kinakain ng lahat ng kuhol?

Hindi lahat! May ilang uri na mandaragit at kumakain ng ibang kuhol o uod, pero karamihan sa kilala natin ay halaman ang kinakain.
copy.bis:
Tanom ra ba ang gikaon sa tanang kuhol?

Dili tanan! Adunay pipila ka matang nga manunukob nga mokaon og laing kuhol o ulod, apan kasagaran sa atong nailhan tanom ra ang ginakaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its sensitive head and tentacles go in first, then its soft foot follows
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card names outer body parts (head, tentacles, foot) but focuses on hiding behavior and protection, not on the role of these parts to move or gather food as required by the competency.

copy.en: When a snail hides, its sensitive head and tentacles go in first, then its soft foot follows — protecting its most important parts!
copy.tl: Kapag nagtatago ang kuhol, unang pumapasok ang sensitibong ulo at sungay nito, saka sumusunod ang malambot na paa — para maprotektahan ang pinakamahalagang bahagi nito!
copy.bis: Kon mutago ang kuhol, ang sensitibo nga ulo ug sungay-sungay maoy unang musulod, dayon mosunod ang humok nga tiil — para mapanalipdan ang labing importante nga bahin niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some snails have a hard lid called an operculum on their foot
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (operculum on the foot) but does not identify its role in movement or gathering food; the stated role is closing the shell opening, which is not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some snails have a hard lid called an operculum on their foot
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The operculum is an adaptation, but the card does not describe how snails have changed to better suit their environment, nor does it use secondary sources or provide an example like mimicry or camouflage. It merely states the structure's function.

copy.en:
What is a snail's little trapdoor?

Some snails have a hard lid called an operculum on their foot — after they pull inside, it closes the shell opening like a little door!
copy.tl:
Ano ang tinatawag na 'pinto' ng kuhol?

May mga kuhol na may matigas na takip na tinatawag na operculum sa likod ng paa nila — kapag pumasok sila sa shell, isinasara nito ang bukana parang pinto!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gitawag nga 'pultahan' sa kuhol?

Adunay mga kuhol nga naa'y gahi nga takip nga gitawag operculum sa likod sa ilang tiil — kon makasulod na sila sa kabhang, gisira niini ang baba sama sa pultahan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most snail shells coil to the right when viewed from the tip
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single trait of snail shells (coiling direction) but does not classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms) using a table. It shares the broad subject of animals but provides no instructional support for classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most snail shells coil to the right when viewed from the tip
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an outer body part (the shell) but does not describe its role in movement or gathering food, which is the focus of the competency. It is only tangentially related to observing animal body parts.

copy.en:
Which way do most snail shells coil?

Most snail shells coil to the right when viewed from the tip — this is called dextral coiling, and only a rare few coil the other way.
copy.tl:
Saang direksyon umiikot ang kabibe ng karamihang kuhol?

Karamihan ng kabibe ng kuhol ay umiikot pakanan kapag tiningnan mula sa tuktok — tinatawag itong dextral, at bihira lang ang umiikot pakaliwa.
copy.bis:
Asa nga direksyon moliko ang kabhang sa kadaghanang kuhol?

Kadaghanan sa kabhang sa kuhol moliko padulong sa tuo kon tan-awon gikan sa tumoy — gitawag kini og dextral, ug talagsa ra ang moliko sa wala.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Snails have simple eyes at the tips of their tentacles, but these only sense light and dark — not clear pictures.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (eyes) and its function (sensing light/dark), but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of body parts to move and to gather food. Sensing light/dark is not movement or food gathering, so it does not directly support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Snails have simple eyes at the tips of their tentacles, but these only sense light and dark — not clear pictures.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a sensory response to light, which is a response, but the competency focuses on the characteristics of living things: grow, respond, and reproduce. The card does not explicitly connect this to the general characteristic of responding, nor does it address growth or reproduction. It is only tangentially related to the concept of responding.

copy.en: Snails have simple eyes at the tips of their tentacles, but these only sense light and dark — not clear pictures.
copy.tl: Ang mga kuhol ay may simpleng mata sa dulo ng kanilang sungay, pero ito'y nakakaramdam lamang ng liwanag at dilim, hindi malinaw na larawan.
copy.bis: Ang mga kuhol adunay simple nga mata sa tumoy sa ilang sungay, apan makabati lang kini sa kahayag ug kangitngit, dili klaro nga hulagway.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A snail moves very slowly, gliding gently along its path.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes the snail's slow gliding movement. It does not mention or describe any outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in moving or gathering food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A snail moves very slowly, gliding gently along its path.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions slow movement but does not define speed as distance traveled over time, nor does it provide any distance or time information needed to identify the concept of speed.

copy.en: A snail moves very slowly, gliding gently along its path.
copy.tl: Napakabagal gumalaw ng kuhol, dahan-dahan itong gumagapang sa daan nito.
copy.bis: Hinay kaayo molihok ang kuhol, hinay-hinay nga nagakamang sa iyang agianan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A cobra bite is treated at the hospital with antivenom, a special medicine that fights the venom in your body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a snakebite and antivenom treatment, which is an example of a harmful interaction between a living thing (snake) and a human, and a remedy. However, it does not explain how interactions between living things or living/non-living things bring good or harm; it merely states a medical fact without addressing the interaction concept or the good/harm framework.

copy.en: A cobra bite is treated at the hospital with antivenom, a special medicine that fights the venom in your body.
copy.tl: Ang kagat ng cobra ay ginagamot sa ospital gamit ang antivenom, isang gamot na pumupuksa sa kamandag.
copy.bis: Ang paak sa cobra tambalan sa ospital pinaagi sa antivenom, usa ka tambal nga mosukol sa hilo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they hide underground and sleep for months — this is called brumation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific winter survival behavior (brumation) of snakes. While this could be interpreted as a response to cold, the competency requires describing the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The card does not explicitly teach 'respond' as a characteristic, nor does it mention growth or reproduction. It is a factual animal-behavior card that shares vocabulary with the competency but does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en:
What do snakes do in winter?

In freezing countries, snakes can't move at all in winter, so they hide underground and sleep for months — this is called brumation.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng ahas sa taglamig?

Sa malamig na bansa, hindi na makakilos ang mga ahas sa taglamig, kaya nagtatago sila sa lupa at natutulog ng ilang buwan — tawag dito ay brumation.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buhaton sa bitin sa tigtugnaw?

Sa bugnaw nga nasod, dili na makalihok ang mga bitin sa tigtugnaw, mao nga motago sila sa yuta ug matulog og pipila ka bulan — gitawag kining brumation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sharp fangs it uses to inject venom
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes fangs as an outer body part of a snake, but their stated role is injecting venom, not moving or gathering food as required by G3-L-4. It shares the broad topic of animal body parts but does not directly support the competency's specific skill.

copy.en: A venomous snake has sharp fangs it uses to inject venom into whatever it bites.
copy.tl: May matutulis na pangil ang makamandag na ahas na ginagamit para iturok ang kamandag sa biktima nito.
copy.bis: Ang makahilo nga bitin adunay talinis nga pangil nga gigamit aron iturok ang hilo ngadto sa biktima niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A snake sheds its skin, leaving behind a thin, dry covering with scale patterns
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes snake skin shedding, which is a fact about a living thing but does not teach the characteristics of growing, responding, or reproducing. It provides no direct instructional support for G3-L-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A snake sheds its skin, leaving behind a thin, dry covering with scale patterns
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a snake, which is a reptile, but it does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups. The required table format is absent, so this is only related to the broad topic of animals.

copy.en:
Why do you find snake skin in grass?

A snake sheds its skin, leaving behind a thin, dry covering with scale patterns — that's why people sometimes spot it in grass or on rocks.
copy.tl:
Bakit may makikitang balat ng ahas sa damuhan?

Naglalabas ang ahas ng manipis at tuyong balat na may guhit ng kaliskis — kaya minsan ito'y natatagpuan sa damuhan o bato.
copy.bis:
Nganong makit-an ang panit sa halas sa sagbot?

Ang halas mohumod og nipis ug uga nga panit nga adunay sundayag sa himbis — mao nga usahay makit-an kini sa sagbot o bato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: some snakes have venom they inject through sharp fangs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fangs as a body part, but the competency requires describing outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement and food gathering. The card does not address movement or food gathering; it focuses on venom injection, which is not the specified role.

copy.en:
Are all snakes venomous?

No! Only some snakes have venom they inject through sharp fangs — many snakes have no venom at all.
copy.tl:
Lahat ba ng ahas ay may kamandag?

Hindi! Ang ilang ahas lang ang may kamandag na ipinapasok sa biktima gamit ang matatalas na pangil — marami sa kanila ay walang lason.
copy.bis:
Tanan ba nga bitin adunay hilo?

Dili! Ang uban ra nga bitin adunay hilo nga ituslok gamit ang hait nga tango — daghan kanila ang walay hilo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One sneeze sprays thousands of tiny germ-filled droplets into the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sneezing and droplets but does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work. It only tangentially relates to the respiratory system through the act of sneezing.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One sneeze sprays thousands of tiny germ-filled droplets into the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses germ transmission via droplets, not the distinction between unicellular and multicellular organisms. No support for the competency about cell organization.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a big reason colds and flu spread fast in a classroom
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies harm from germs spreading between people, but it does not explain interactions between living things or between living and non-living things bringing good or harm. It only states a fact about disease spread without explaining the interaction mechanism.

copy.en: One sneeze sprays thousands of tiny germ-filled droplets into the air — a big reason colds and flu spread fast in a classroom.
copy.tl: Ang isang bahin ay nagpapakalat ng libu-libong maliliit na patak na puno ng mikrobyo sa hangin — isa itong dahilan kung bakit mabilis kumalat ang sipon at trangkaso sa silid-aralan.
copy.bis: Ang usa ka bahaon mopakatap og liboan ka gagmayng tulo nga puno sa mikrobyo ngadto sa hangin — usa kini ka rason nganong paspas mokatap ang sip-on ug trangkaso sa klasehanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each snowflake is an ice crystal that almost always has six sides or six branches
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a solid (ice crystal) and its shape, but does not describe the general properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. It only gives a specific fact about snowflakes, not the competency's concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each snowflake is an ice crystal that almost always has six sides or six branches
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) or use diagrams/flowcharts. It is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each snowflake is an ice crystal that almost always has six sides or six branches
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a physical property (six sides) of a solid material, but does not describe the general physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. It is a specific example, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en: Each snowflake is an ice crystal that almost always has six sides or six branches, making them look like tiny stars!
copy.tl: Ang bawat butil ng snowflake ay isang kristal ng yelo na halos laging may anim na sulok o sanga, kaya parang maliliit na bituin!
copy.bis: Ang matag butil sa snowflake usa ka kristal sa yelo nga halos kanunay adunay unom ka kilid o sanga, mao nga sama sila sa gagmay nga bituon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: mixing animal fat, water, and wood ash (which holds natural lye) created a slippery, cleaning substance.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out a valid and reliable scientific investigation to show the formation of a new substance, such as formation of a carbonate (carbon dioxide in limewater), or formation of a precipitate (from silver nitrate solution)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a historical discovery of soap from mixing fat, water, and ash, but does not involve carrying out a valid and reliable scientific investigation, nor does it address the specific examples (carbonate formation or precipitate formation) in the competency. It only mentions a substance being formed, without any investigation process.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: mixing animal fat, water, and wood ash (which holds natural lye) created a slippery, cleaning substance.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the indicators for a chemical reaction as color change, the formation of a precipitate, the release of gas, and or odor, or a change in temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a new substance (soap) being formed, but does not describe any of the indicators for a chemical reaction (color change, precipitate, gas release, odor, or temperature change). It is a historical anecdote about soap discovery, not a description of reaction indicators.

copy.en: Thousands of years ago, people discovered soap! They noticed that mixing animal fat, water, and wood ash (which holds natural lye) created a slippery, cleaning substance.
copy.tl: Libong taon na ang nakalipas, natuklasan ng mga tao ang sabon! Napansin nilang ang paghahalo ng taba ng hayop, tubig, at abo ng kahoy (may natural na lihiya) ay gumagawa ng madulas na panlinis.
copy.bis: Libo ka tuig na ang milabay, nadiskubrehan sa mga tawo ang sabon! Namatikdan nila nga ang pagsagol sa tambok sa hayop, tubig, ug abo sa kahoy (adunay natural nga lihiya) naghimo og madanlog nga panlimpyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Since soap grabs oil, washing too much or using harsh soap can strip the natural oil protecting our skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses soap removing natural oil from skin, which is a practical/health observation, not a description of chemical properties of materials such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. It shares vocabulary (soap, oil) but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Since soap grabs oil, washing too much or using harsh soap can strip the natural oil protecting our skin. That's why skin gets dry, itchy, or cracked — and why we sometimes need lotion after!
copy.tl: Dahil hinahawakan ng sabon ang langis, sobrang paghuhugas o matapang na sabon ay nagtatanggal ng natural na langis na nagpoprotekta sa balat. Kaya natutuyo, nangangati, o napuputok ang balat — kaya minsan kailangan ng lotion!
copy.bis: Tungod kay gikuptan sa sabon ang lana, ang sobra nga paghugas o kusog nga sabon nagtangtang sa natural nga lana nga nagpanalipod sa panit. Mao nga mauga, makatol, o mabuak ang panit — busa usahay kinahanglan og lotion!
